items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: when I went to this other music house, which the staff was J.J. Johnson, me and Tommy Newsom

ctx.x: Well how much input did you have like an ad agency would come to you and say we have to do an ad for toilet paper. Did they — was it your job to think of a melody?

Okay, I worked in a music house with this guy who started a music production company so he would basically write the melodies, he would show them to me and maybe I’d fix something here and there. And then I would orchestrate. So yeah, when I went to this other music house, which the staff was J.J. Johnson, me and Tommy Newsom, which was a great staff, if you can imagine us all in one building together, it was great. There I was ©Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

in charge of composing. Because the guy who ran the studio, he was the business end. He didn’t do any actual writing so I would be composing more melodies. But you know again, they give you an outline or storyboard to work with and you’d start writing. Like you might write five or six little ditties. Go into the studio and just record some demos for them to listen to. And they’ll say well I like this one.
